library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

candidate_paths <- c(
  "C:/Users/analyst/Desktop/nhanes_equity_v6.csv",
  "examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv",
  "../../../examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv"
)

data_path <- candidate_paths[file.exists(candidate_paths)][1]
if (is.na(data_path)) {
  stop("Could not find nhanes_equity_v6.csv")
}

nhanes <- read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

cycle_levels <- sort(unique(nhanes$Cycle))
endpoint_cycles <- c(cycle_levels[1], cycle_levels[length(cycle_levels)])

# Select NHANES cycles approximately every 5 years
cycle_levels <- sort(unique(as.character(nhanes$Cycle)))

selected_cycles <- cycle_levels[
  seq(1, length(cycle_levels), by = 2)
]

# Calculate mean BMI for each income group and cycle
improved_summary <- nhanes |>
  filter(
    !is.na(BMI),
    !is.na(IncomeGroup),
    Cycle %in% selected_cycles
  ) |>
  group_by(Cycle, IncomeGroup) |>
  summarise(
    mean_bmi = mean(BMI),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Create improved scatter plot
improved_plot <- ggplot(
  improved_summary,
  aes(x = Cycle, y = mean_bmi, color = IncomeGroup)
) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = selected_cycles) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(20, 30)) +
  labs(
    title = "Trends in Mean BMI Among U.S. Adults by Income Group",
    subtitle = "Mean BMI across selected NHANES cycles",
    x = "NHANES cycle",
    y = "Mean BMI (kg/m²)",
    color = "Income group"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)+
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

print(improved_plot)

ggsave(
  "assignments/assignment05-visualization/submission/corrected-plot.png",
  plot = last_plot(),
  width = 7,
  height = 5
)

#What I revised and why
I revised the graph by including more NHANES cycles to better illustrate changes in mean BMI across income groups over time. I replaced the dashed lines with a scatter plot to avoid implying continuous trends between observations and adjusted the x-axis labels to improve readability. I also expanded the y-axis range to avoid exaggerating differences in BMI between income groups. Finally, I revised the title to use neutral language and avoid making unsupported causal claims.
